prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (max 500 words)

- Economic and fiscal policy: Maintain low inflation (2% target) and fiscal rules (borrow to invest; keep net debt prudent). No rises in basic/top income tax; no VAT on essentials. Continue efficiency savings to fund frontline services. Support enterprise via low corporation and capital gains taxes, R&D credits, science strategy to raise R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014, and skills/apprenticeships reform. Goal of high employment with welfare-to-work, incapacity benefit reform, and minimum wage increases. Modernise regulation and planning; promote competition and an EU single market in services. Energy policy to balance climate goals and security with a mixed generation portfolio and renewables growth.

- Transport: Over £180bn public investment to 2015; rail reliability upgrades, consider high-speed rail and Crossrail; targeted motorway capacity/management; examine national road pricing; free off-peak local bus travel for over-60s and disabled; stronger local powers over buses; promote cycling/walking; include aviation in EU emissions trading; expand shipping and ports.

- Regional, equality and rural: Strengthen Regional Development Agencies and deprived neighbourhoods initiatives. Enforce equality laws (gender, race, disability, religion, sexual orientation; age from 2006). Promote disabled people’s personalised support. Rural measures for schools, post offices, buses, affordable housing, CAP and fisheries reform, environmental stewardship, biomass/biofuels, Animal Welfare Bill.

- Education and skills: Personalised learning; literacy/numeracy targets; workforce development; multi-year funding with a dedicated national schools budget and stronger governance. Primary and secondary rebuild (Building Schools for the Future); every secondary to be a specialist school; expand academies (aim 200 by 2010) with fair admissions; stronger discipline and alternative provision; balanced SEN offer. 14–19 reform with specialised diplomas, more apprenticeships, EMAs, FE transformation and skills academies. Higher education funding reform with fees capped at £3,000 (inflation-linked), expanded bursaries, 50% participation aim, more PhD support. Children’s Trusts to integrate services.

- Crime, policing and justice: Neighbourhood policing teams nationwide by 2010; more Community Support Officers; single non-emergency number. Stronger tools against antisocial behaviour and alcohol-related disorder. Expand youth interventions and drug treatment with compulsory testing/assessment for relevant offenders; establish Serious Organised Crime Agency. Tougher controls on guns/knives; stronger sentencing for serious offences; universal post-release supervision and expanded tagging; offender management focused on reducing reoffending; share seized criminal assets with local agencies. Corporate manslaughter offence; fraud trial reforms; better victim/witness support and restorative justice.

- Migration, borders, security: Points-based immigration favouring skills; English tests for permanent settlement; civil penalties for employing illegal workers; biometric visas, e-borders, and ID cards linked to passport renewal. Faster, fairer asylum decisions. New terrorism offences and control orders alongside prosecution.

- NHS and public health: Major investment, staff expansion, shorter waits (maximum 18 weeks from referral to treatment by 2008), patient choice of hospital, expand primary/community care (including community hospitals), GP commissioning, independent/voluntary capacity where needed; strengthen hygiene and clinical governance; reduce bureaucracy. Dentistry expansion/review. Public health: stronger school food standards, clearer food labelling, curb marketing to children, expanded smoking restrictions and cessation support, school nurses, health trainers.

- Older people: Pension Credit increases to 2007–08; universal benefits (fuel, bus travel), fuel poverty targets; long-term pensions settlement following commission review; more member-nominated trustees; flexible retirement rights; pilot individual care budgets.

- Families, childcare, housing: Target to halve child poverty by 2010–11; increase Child Tax Credit; Child Trust Fund growth options. Universal early years via Sure Start Children’s Centres in every community by 2010; extend free nursery hours and wraparound childcare to age 14; greater childcare cost support; extend flexible working (consult on carers); expand mediation and enforce access orders. Increase home ownership (stamp duty threshold raised), shared ownership, growth areas investment; increase new social homes by 50% by 2008; choice-based lettings.

- International: Active EU role and reform; NATO central to defence; euro decision subject to economic tests and referendum. Counter-proliferation; support peace processes (e.g., Middle East); maintain independent nuclear deterrent; modernise armed forces; prioritise veterans. UN, IFIs and humanitarian system reform. Climate leadership (Kyoto targets, 20% CO2 cut by 2010; 60% by 2050), renewables and efficiency; Africa focus with increased aid (0.7% GNI by 2013), debt relief, governance, universal access to AIDS treatment by 2010; fairer trade, end agricultural export subsidies by 2010.

- Culture, sport, media, digital, environment: Sustained arts funding; free national museums; regional museum renewal; Creative Sparks in schools; community sports facilities, school sport entitlements, National Sports Foundation; support 2012 Olympics bid. BBC governance reform (BBC Trust), guaranteed licence fee; digital switchover 2008–2012; close digital divide; modernise IP; film tax relief. Clean neighbourhoods powers; universal kerbside recycling of at least two materials by 2010; sustainable building code; Marine Act; protect green belt and promote brownfield.

- Democracy and devolution: Complete House of Lords reform (remove remaining hereditary peers, time limits on bills, codify conventions, free vote on composition); review electoral systems via referendum for Westminster; strengthen party finance oversight; Single Equality Act and new Equality/Human Rights Commission. Further devolution to Wales, London and regions; restore Northern Ireland institutions conditional on ending paramilitarism. Empower neighbourhoods and parish councils, expand social enterprise/charities role, youth volunteering framework, cut council bureaucracy, three-year settlements, consider elected mayors, control excessive council tax increases and improve benefit take-up.
</text>
